name: Toleda & Vasquez Ceremonial Robe
description:
Toleda & Vasquez has been dressing the ceremonial functions of GLMZ's major corponations for forty years — investitures, board ascensions, quarterly observances, and the various ritual moments that corporate culture has developed to replace older forms of meaning-making. Their ceremonial robe is a full-length, wide-sleeved garment in heavy damask-weave synthetic, with each commission produced in the client corporation's specific colorway and embroidered with their iconographic marks. The robe closes at the center front with a series of fabric-covered buttons and is cut with enough volume to be worn over formal attire.

Off the custom commission circuit, Toleda & Vasquez produces a 'civic' version in neutral deep burgundy and navy that is used by GLMZ's civil governance apparatus, cultural institutions, and a small number of religious and philosophical communities. This version is available to order by any Tier 3 or above buyer, though wearing one without institutional affiliation is considered eccentric at best. It is extraordinarily well-made and will outlast most of the people who wear it.
what_it_says: You represent something larger than yourself — an institution, a corporation, a community. Or you want to.
worn_by: the very occasionally eccentric wealthy individual
story_hooks: A ceremonial robe commissioned for a corponation's board ascension ceremony was stolen before the event — the new executive refuses to proceed without it, claiming it was meant to contain something sewn into the lining
The civic version has been adopted by a new philosophical movement whose beliefs are considered destabilizing by at least two corponations
Toleda & Vasquez keeps meticulous records of every commission — their archive, if accessed, would be a map of every major power ceremony in GLMZ for four decades
